turns.user: Show me published prints similar to an 800 mm high wall printed with a 25 mm nozzle and 15 mm layers.
turns.text:
I’ll search the published print runs for walls near 800 mm high with nozzle and layer dimensions close to yours, then report the closest documented examples.
The similarity tool requires a layer cycle time, which you haven’t specified. I’ll inspect the print-run records directly so the comparison doesn’t depend on an assumed printing schedule.
The closest documented wall prints match your **25 mm nozzle and 15 mm layers**, but reached **390 mm**, below your 800 mm target.

| Published print | Nozzle / layer | Reported height | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| [RBA-3DPC façade section](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clema.2022.100090) | 25 / 15 mm | 390 mm | Printed successfully; 26 layers |
| [RBA-3DPC and PCM-3DPC façade sections](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2023.136247) | 25 / 15 mm | 390 mm | Both printed successfully; 26 layers each |
| [Concrete wall specimens](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cscm.2024.e02892) | 15 / 10 mm | 800 mm | Printed successfully |
| [PG geopolymer wall](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.addma.2024.104462) | 20 / 13 mm | 1,150 mm | No failure before the printhead reached its travel limit |
| [H-3 wall buildability test](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2025.141735) | 20 / 10 mm | 730 mm | Collapsed at the reported final height |

In the indexed records with reported wall height, the **25 mm / 15 mm combination appears in three runs across two papers; the greatest reported height is 390 mm**. The taller examples show that wall height depends on the material and printing setup as well as nozzle and layer size, so they do not establish that your proposed wall will be buildable.

sample.notes: Buildability test (R1/R2) and single-filament nozzle-diameter test (R4/R5) matched to test_uid T2 (merged 'other' family test covering buildability, CO2 uptake, BET and interfacial bending; see record unmapped_terms UM3). Rheology thixotropy (3-step shear rate 0.1/100/0.1 s-1) and shear-thinning sweep (0.1-150 s-1) protocols are described only qualitatively in the paper (percent recovery, relative stiffness) and are NOT captured as a test row in the record (extraction_notes T6: figure series not digitised) - both rheology_protocols rows carry test_uid: null. shear_rate_s1 left null for the flow-curve-fit sweep because it spans a range (0.1-150 s-1), not a single stated rate. No print speed (mm/s) or layer cycle time is stated anywhere in the accessible text. R4/R5 (single-filament nozzle test) report a nozzle-diameter range (2-21 mm) rather than a single run setting; run-level nozzle diameter fields are not part of this schema (only printer.nozzle_d_mm, set to the 4.8 mm nozzle used for the main structures) so the range is described in the quote instead. No units required conversion.

No rheology (yield-stress/viscosity/Athix) test protocol reported; ink flow properties are only described qualitatively ('proper flow properties... shape holding'), no instrument/protocol named, so rheology_protocols is empty and matches the record's test list (flexural only). print_speed_mm_s converted from 250 mm/min to mm/s by /60 (=4.17). Pitch angle for the smallest Bouligand category is given as psi=2 degrees in the introductory list of architectures but as psi=8 degrees in the Results paragraph reporting pitch angles studied (8,15,30,45,90); likely an OCR/typo discrepancy in the source text, both values are quoted verbatim, neither is treated as authoritative. No print failures, buildability tests, or stack-to-failure trials are reported anywhere in the paper; all printed architectures proceed directly to post-cure mechanical testing, so all runs are labelled printable on the general author statement that these elements were 'achieved by 3D-printing'. The figures directory for this paper contains only manuscript text page scans (page_01..page_41.png); no distinct figure graphics with captions were found in the 3 pages sampled (pp. 2, 17, 18), so figures did not add information beyond the body text.

No printing experiment reported: the paper investigates carbon-fiber-tape reinforcement 'for' 3D concrete printing but the four-point-bending test specimens (series 1-4) were cast in moulds per DIN EN 12390-2 ('The production and storage of the test specimens is carried out according to the standard DIN EN 12390-2'), not additively manufactured; no printer, nozzle, or print settings are mentioned anywhere in the text. The record's only test (T1, flexure_four_point) is a hardened-concrete mechanical test, not a fresh-state rheology test, so rheology_protocols is empty; no yield-stress/viscosity/Athix test is reported for the fine-grained concrete mix either.

input.sql: SELECT r.paper_uid,r.run_id,r.mix_name_in_paper,r.object,COALESCE(r.nozzle_d_mm,p.nozzle_d_mm) AS nozzle_d_mm,r.layer_height_mm,r.n_layers_achieved,r.height_achieved_mm,r.outcome,r.printability_label,r.failure_mode,r.print_speed_mm_s,r.layer_cycle_time_s,r.source_locator,r.quote FROM print_runs r LEFT JOIN printers p ON p.paper_uid=r.paper_uid WHERE lower(r.object) LIKE '%wall%' AND r.height_achieved_mm IS NOT NULL AND r.layer_height_mm IS NOT NULL AND COALESCE(r.nozzle_d_mm,p.nozzle_d_mm) IS NOT NULL ORDER BY ABS(r.height_achieved_mm-800)/800.0 + ABS(COALESCE(r.nozzle_d_mm,p.nozzle_d_mm)-25)/25.0 + ABS(r.layer_height_mm-15)/15.0 LIMIT 30

input.sql: SELECT r.paper_uid,r.run_id,r.mix_name_in_paper,r.object,COALESCE(r.nozzle_d_mm,p.nozzle_d_mm) AS nozzle_mm,r.layer_height_mm AS layer_mm,r.height_achieved_mm AS height_mm,r.outcome,r.failure_mode,r.print_speed_mm_s,r.layer_cycle_time_s,r.source_locator FROM print_runs r LEFT JOIN printers p ON p.paper_uid=r.paper_uid WHERE lower(r.object) LIKE '%wall%' AND r.height_achieved_mm BETWEEN 650 AND 1300 AND r.layer_height_mm BETWEEN 8 AND 20 AND COALESCE(r.nozzle_d_mm,p.nozzle_d_mm) BETWEEN 15 AND 40 ORDER BY ABS(r.height_achieved_mm-800) + 10*ABS(COALESCE(r.nozzle_d_mm,p.nozzle_d_mm)-25) + 10*ABS(r.layer_height_mm-15) LIMIT 20

rows.quote: 'using a circular printing nozzle with a diameter of 15 mm to maintain a printing speed of 10 cm/s, the height of the printed filaments is 10 mm and the width is 20 mm.' 'Printing one layer of each wall is a cycle, and the thickness of the printed layer is 10 mm. After finishing the concrete with a height of 400 mm, it is necessary to scrape the printing path with a spatula... When the wall is printed to a suitable height, place the pre-welded steel mesh manually... Half an hour after the wall printing is completed, place vertical steel bars in the reserved steel bar holes.' Table 4: all 10 wall specimens printed to a height of 800 mm (width 800/1000 mm, thickness 160 mm).
rows.source_locator: Section 2.1 Mix proportion; Section 2.4 Construction procedure; Table 4; Fig. 6

rows.quote: 'PC and PG were used to print wall structures (Fig. 4) with the same layouts (w ≈ 6.5 cm, L ≈ 120 cm) using the same printing parameters (t_l = 22 s, h_l = 1.3 cm, v_H = 0.55 mm/s). The printing process continued until structural failure occurred during the experiments.' 'In contrast, due to the rapid hardening characteristics of geopolymer, PG did not experience any failure even when printed to a vertical height of 1.15 m. It is worth noting that 1.15 m is the mechanical displacement limit of the printhead, thus the printing process had to be terminated. Although the PG printed structure did not experience failure, it still serves as strong empirical evidence supporting the better performance of AIOM.'
